intended_object: The functorial map T_p(f) : T_p A → T_p B that a group homomorphism f : A → B induces on p-adic Tate modules. It sends a compatible family (x_n) to (f(x_n)). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition applies f at each level: `levelMap f n` restricts f to a map A[p^n] → B[p^n]. Applying this to each component of x gives an element of the product of the groups B[p^n]. The proof checks that this family is compatible, since p • f(x_{n+1}) = f(p • x_{n+1}) = f(x_n). The family therefore lies in `tateModuleSubgroup p B`. This is exactly the standard induced map on inverse limits. The library also proves that it respects identities and compositions (`map_id` and the lemma after it).

The generality is natural: A and B are arbitrary additive commutative groups and p is any natural number, matching the library's definition of `TateModule`. Mathlib has no Tate module, so there is no counterpart.
